raw_case_text: A 68-year-old male presented with a 2.0x0.7 cm crusted keratotic plaque on his left infraorbital area that was concerning for nonmelanoma skin cancer. An H&E-stained section of a shave-biopsy revealed granulomatous inflammation with pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia and a few yeast with narrow-based budding suggestive of H. capsulatum. Urine testing for H. capsulatum antigen was negative. This lesion resolved within 2 weeks without medical intervention. Chest radiographs revealed small minimally calcified lymph nodes in the inferior right hilum and subcarinal chain (Fig. 1). One year later, the patient presented with recurrence of the lesion as a 2.0x1.0 cm thin, irritated, erythematous and crusted plaque (Fig. 2). No preceding trauma nor recent change in health status nor medications were reported. A full-skin examination demonstrated no similar lesions. Repeat biopsy was performed and showed findings similar to those previously described; however, numerous yeast forms were noted in this specimen (Fig. 3a, b). The organisms were highlighted by periodic acid-Schiff (PAS) and Grocott-Gomori methenamine silver (GMS) stains (Fig. 3c, d). Negative Fontana-Masson and mucicarmine stains excluded the presence of a Cryptococcus sp. Overall, the morphological appearance and the results of the special histological stains were consistent with those expected for H. capsulatum infection. Extensive microbiological testing, including Histoplasma H and M bands via immunodiffusion, urine Histoplasma antigen, Histoplasma mycelia complement fixation, Histoplasma yeast complement fixation, serum Blastomyces antigen and antibody, serum Aspergillus antibody, serum Coccidian antibody, and serum HIV antibodies and antigens were unrevealing. Cultivation of an aetiological agent was hampered by mishandling of the specimen prior to its receipt by the laboratory. A respiratory culture was not performed given significant delays in scheduling. Next-generation nucleic acid sequencing (NGS) of a 230 bp region of the internal transcribed spacer (ITS) that was amplified from the tissue block confirmed the presence of H. capsulatum. NGS was performed using an iSeq100 system (Illumina). Sequence data were analysed using an online database (ITS metagenomics app v. 1.1.0 at BaseSpace Sequence Hub). The patient was prescribed and started treatment with 200 mg itraconazole daily for a duration of 1 year and, to date, he has not reported recrudescence of the infection 8 months following his second biopsy.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 68-year-old male presented with a recurrent 2.0 x 1.0 cm erythematous crusted keratotic plaque on his left infraorbital cheek 1 year after spontaneous resolution of a similar lesion at the same site.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: One year earlier, the patient had presented with a 2.0 x 0.7 cm left infraorbital crusted keratotic plaque that spontaneously resolved within 2 weeks after shave biopsy. He re-presented 1 year later with local recurrence of a 2.0 x 1.0 cm thin, irritated, erythematous crusted plaque at the same left infraorbital site without preceding trauma, systemic symptoms, or medication changes.
subjective.past_medical_history: Unremarkable past medical history; no recent trauma or medication changes.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for recurrent left infraorbital crusted skin plaque. Negative for systemic or respiratory symptoms.

objective.physical_examination: A single 2.0 x 1.0 cm thin, irritated, erythematous, crusted keratotic plaque in the left infraorbital region, with no other lesions on full-body skin examination.
objective.routine_investigations: Chest radiograph showed small minimally calcified right inferior hilar and subcarinal lymph nodes. Urine Histoplasma antigen, serum Histoplasma immunodiffusion (H and M bands) and yeast/mycelial complement fixation, Blastomyces antigen/antibody, Aspergillus antibody, Coccidioides antibody, and HIV Ag/Ab tests were all negative.
objective.advanced_workup: Initial and repeat left infraorbital skin shave biopsies demonstrated granulomatous inflammation with pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia and numerous narrow-based budding intracellular/extracellular yeast forms highlighted by PAS and Grocott-Gomori methenamine silver (GMS) stains, with negative Fontana-Masson and mucicarmine stains excluding Cryptococcus spp. Next-generation sequencing (Illumina iSeq100) of a 230 bp internal transcribed spacer (ITS) amplicon from the formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded tissue block confirmed Histoplasma capsulatum.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis of primary/isolated cutaneous histoplasmosis of the left infraorbital cheek mimicking nonmelanoma skin cancer in an immunocompetent host, confirmed by skin biopsy PAS and GMS histopathology and targeted ITS next-generation sequencing identifying Histoplasma capsulatum, while Cryptococcus spp. was excluded by negative mucicarmine and Fontana-Masson staining. Treated with oral itraconazole 200 mg daily for a planned 1-year course, with complete clearance and no recurrence at 8-month follow-up.
